spec:
# Fix The Bb And Or Steel Browser Plugins So That

## Request

> Fix the BB and/or Steel Browser plugins so that when an agent tells the user to sign in using the embedded Steel browser and emits the Steel browser surface directive, the browser is actually shown in the thread UI, as expected in the supplied screenshot context. Trace the directive/rendering integration, implement the appropriate fix, add focused regression coverage, and verify the relevant plugin checks and UI behavior.

## Goal

Whenever an agent asks the user to interact with the project Steel browser,
the same assistant message renders the native inline Steel viewer so the user
has an actual place to complete the requested sign-in, MFA, or manual action.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [AC-1] The Steel agent instructions require `::steel-browser{}` on its
  own line in the same assistant message whenever the agent asks the user for
  browser interaction, credentials, sign-in, MFA, or another manual handoff.
- [ ] [AC-2] The bundled Steel skill carries the same requirement and forbids
  referring to an embedded browser "above" unless that response contains the
  native directive.
- [ ] [AC-3] Focused regression tests fail if either contributed instructions
  or the bundled skill loses the same-message human-handoff requirement.
- [ ] [AC-UI-1] [UI] A rendered `::steel-browser{}` directive continues to
  mount the existing Steel inline browser without changing its viewer,
  authentication, session, or responsive behavior.
- [ ] [AC-4] Dockside's root-card layout regression assertion matches the
  existing two-column grid (`col-start-2`) and the focused Dockside test passes
  without changing Dockside runtime source or UI behavior.

## Scope

Steel Browser's contributed agent instructions, bundled skill, focused
distribution tests, documentation wording where needed, and the single stale
Dockside source-contract assertion blocking repository CI.

## Non-goals

Changing BB's generic directive parser, opening an external browser, exposing
CDP or Connect URLs, automating credentials or MFA, changing Steel provisioning,
redesigning the existing inline viewer, or changing Dockside runtime components,
styles, layout, or behavior.

## Verification

Run the Steel Browser focused tests, type checking, plugin build/check, and the
existing inline browser check when its project Steel dependency is available.
Confirm the instruction regression assertions cover sign-in and MFA handoffs.
Run the focused Dockside layout test and full pull-request CI after aligning its
stale grid-column assertion with the current component source.

## Risks

Agent instruction adherence is probabilistic, so the requirement must be short,
unambiguous, repeated in both injected instructions and the skill, and protected
by exact regression assertions. The change must not suggest that a directive
alone proves the viewer or BB Connect authentication is healthy.
The integration repair must remain test-only: changing Dockside runtime code
would expand the behavioral surface and require separate UI verification.

## Capability Deltas

See `deltas/steel-browser-viewer.md` and
`deltas/dockside-thread-management.md`.

requirements.name: Root family cards have exactly two semantic rows
requirements.contents:
### Requirement: Root family cards have exactly two semantic rows

Every root MUST render exactly two compact fixed rows using the existing
two-column grid. Row one MUST contain the family state/activity icon, truncated
title, and far-right elapsed time. Row two MUST contain truncated branch text
and one shrink-resistant right cluster with the readable state badge, root-only
PR metadata, and child disclosure/count plus provider identity. Children MUST
never render PR metadata. Ambiguous icons MUST offer hover and keyboard-focus
help. Source-contract tests MUST describe the current two-column placement and
MUST NOT require an obsolete third grid column.

#### Scenario: Repository CI validates the current root-card grid

- **Given** the runtime root card places its metadata cluster in grid column 2
- **When** the Dockside source-contract test runs
- **Then** the assertion expects `col-start-2`
- **And** no Dockside runtime component, styling, layout, or behavior changes

requirements.name: Render the viewer for every human browser handoff
requirements.contents:
### Requirement: Render the viewer for every human browser handoff

Steel SHALL instruct agents to emit `::steel-browser{}` on its own line in the
same assistant message whenever they ask the user to interact with the browser,
including credential entry, sign-in, MFA, consent, or any other manual step.
Agents SHALL NOT refer to an embedded browser "above" unless the current
response contains the directive. This requirement SHALL be present in both the
always-injected plugin instructions and the bundled Steel skill.

#### Scenario: Website requires sign-in

- **GIVEN** the agent has navigated the project Steel session to a sign-in page
- **WHEN** the agent asks the user to enter credentials
- **THEN** that same assistant message contains `::steel-browser{}` on its own line
- **AND** BB renders the native inline Steel viewer with the request
- **AND** the agent does not request credentials in chat

#### Scenario: Website requires MFA after an earlier viewer message

- **GIVEN** an earlier assistant message rendered the Steel viewer
- **WHEN** a later response asks the user to complete MFA or another manual step
- **THEN** the later response repeats `::steel-browser{}` on its own line
- **AND** the user is not told to use an absent or stale browser surface

#### Scenario: Viewer authentication is unavailable

- **WHEN** the native directive renders but BB Connect authentication blocks it
- **THEN** the agent reports that limitation
- **AND** the agent does not open an external browser or expose a viewer URL

decisions:
# Decisions

## D-001: Fix instruction emission, not BB directive rendering

Status: Accepted

### Evidence

`plugins/steel-browser/app.tsx` already registers the `steel-browser` message
directive and mounts `SteelBrowserDirective`. The screenshot's assistant
message contains no visible `::steel-browser{}` directive.

### Options

- Change BB's generic directive parser.
- Add a second automatic viewer surface.
- Make Steel's handoff instruction unambiguous.

### Chosen approach

Make the server instruction and bundled skill require the directive in the same
handoff response.

### Trade-offs and risks

This relies on model adherence, but avoids changing shared BB rendering and
preserves authentication and session boundaries.

### Verification

Distribution tests assert the same-message rule in both instruction surfaces.

## D-002: Preserve the existing viewer

Status: Accepted

### Evidence

Focused inline browser tests already cover desktop/mobile layout, iframe
lifecycle, minimizing, reconnecting, and thread following.

### Options

- Change the existing directive component or CSS.
- Keep the viewer unchanged and fix only when the directive is emitted.

### Chosen approach

Make no component or CSS changes.

### Trade-offs and risks

The fix does not repair a BB Connect outage; it ensures the viewer is requested
and rendered whenever the directive is present.

### Verification

Retain the existing inline browser test as the UI regression check and run
plugin build/type checks.

## D-003: Repair the stale Dockside assertion without changing its UI

Status: Accepted

### Evidence

`plugins/dockside/components/inbox/thread-card.tsx` uses a two-column grid and
places the metadata cluster at `col-start-2`. The failing source-contract test
alone still expects `col-start-3`.

### Options

- Change the runtime component back to a nonexistent third column.
- Update the stale test assertion to describe the current component.

### Chosen approach

Update only the test regex from `col-start-3` to `col-start-2`.

### Trade-offs and risks

This restores CI coverage without changing the shipped Dockside interface.

### Verification

Run the focused Dockside test and then the full pull-request CI workflow.
